By Lemma <a href="#lem:additive-deletion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:additive-deletion">19</a>, it suffices to put a small set of vertices in $X$ and show that the remaining footprint $Y$ is $O(t)$-degenerate and that every vertex outside $X\cup Y$ has $O(t)$ neighbors in $Y$.

Throughout this section put $$m_0=\left\lceil(\log t)^2\right\rceil,\qquad
 R_t=\frac{m_0(m_0+1)}2.$$ We take $t$ sufficiently large that $m_0\le t$. For a family of paths $\mathcal Q$, write $V(\mathcal Q)$ for the union of their vertex sets.

<a id="stmt-separate-footprint"></a>
<div id="separate:footprint" class="lemma">

**Lemma 35** (Deleting a history of paths). *Let $h(G)<t$. Start with $F_0=W_0$, where $|W_0|=t$, and perform at most $R_t$ rounds with the following rules. At the start of a round there is a footprint $F$ and a set $W\subseteq F$ of $t$ tips.*

1.  *Choose disjoint sets $J,D\subseteq V(G)\setminus F$, each of size at most $t^{1.06}$, and a set $R\subseteq J$ of at most $t$ vertices. Put $Z=W\cup R$.*

2.  *In the induced graph $G-(F\setminus W)$, choose a minimum-total-length double system $\mathcal Q_1$ from $Z$ to $D$: two paths from each vertex of $Z$, otherwise vertex-disjoint, with distinct target ends. Set $$F^- =F\cup J\cup D\cup V(\mathcal Q_1).$$*

3.  *Choose a source set $A\subseteq V(G)\setminus F^-$. In the induced graph $G-(F\cup R)$, choose a minimum-total-length system $\mathcal Q_2$ of $2t$ vertex-disjoint paths from arbitrary distinct vertices of $A$ to arbitrary distinct vertices of $D$. Set $$F^+=F^-\cup V(\mathcal Q_2),$$ and choose $t$ tips $W^+\subseteq F^+$ for the next round.*

*Only histories in which the indicated systems exist are considered. The final round may end after step <span class="upright">(ii)</span>.*

<a id="separate:cf"></a>
*There is an absolute integer $$\label{separate:cf}
 c_f=c_{6B_*+20}=4L+6B_*+25$$ such that, for all sufficiently large $t$, every final footprint $F_{\rm last}$ of such a history satisfies $$\ell(G-F_{\rm last})\ge\ell(G)-c_ft.$$ The same assertion holds for the initial footprint.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-separate-footprint"><summary>Proof of stmt-separate-footprint</summary>

*Proof.* We use $c_d$ from Lemma <a href="#lem:additive-deletion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:additive-deletion">19</a> and $B_*$ from Lemma <a href="#lem:incidence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:incidence">21</a>. All constants and cutoffs in this proof are independent of the history and of the lengths of its paths.

<a id="pm-h-22"></a>
###### The two path collections.

Remove the starting vertex from each first-system path, and collect all the resulting nonempty paths in a family $\mathcal A$. These paths are pairwise vertex-disjoint. Within one round the only intersections of first-system paths are their prescribed starts, which have been removed. Across rounds, a new first system avoids the old footprint except at its tips $W$. Every tip is a prescribed start, and no such start is internal on any path of the system. After stripping starts, the new paths therefore avoid the entire old footprint.

<a id="separate:path-count"></a>
Let $\mathcal B$ consist of the full second-system paths from all rounds. These too are pairwise vertex-disjoint: each new second system avoids the entire old footprint, which contains every earlier second-system path. No disjointness between $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ is asserted or needed. There are at most $4t$ first paths and $2t$ second paths per round, so, if $q\le R_t$ rounds have been started, $$\label{separate:path-count}
 |\mathcal A|+|\mathcal B|\le6tq\le6tR_t.$$

<a id="pm-h-23"></a>
###### Small sets and exceptional vertices.

Let $X_0$ contain all districts $J,D$, all tip sets appearing in the history, and the ends of every path in both systems. Counting repetitions only increases the following bound: <a id="separate:x0"></a>$$\label{separate:x0}
 |X_0|\le 2R_t t^{1.06}+(13R_t+1)t.$$ Indeed, there are at most $R_t+1$ tip sets; the two systems together have at most $12t$ path-end occurrences per round.

Consider the footprints at the start of each round and also $F_{\rm last}$; call these at most $R_t+1$ sets the snapshots. The final snapshot will control neighbors of vertices outside the final footprint. Earlier snapshots will control the neighbors that a newly entering vertex has on older paths. At a snapshot $T$, let $\mathcal A_T,\mathcal B_T$ be the two collections formed by systems already included in $T$. They use the original recorded paths, with only each first path’s own start removed; no vertices of the set $X$ defined below have yet been removed from these collections. For either collection $\mathcal C$, declare a vertex $v\in V(G)\setminus T$ exceptional if it has a neighbor on at least $B_*t$ distinct members of $\mathcal C$.

<a id="separate:x-bound"></a>
To count these vertices, contract the disjoint connected paths of $\mathcal C$ to a set of $|\mathcal C|$ vertices. Vertices outside $T$ are not contracted. Their numbers of distinct neighbors in the contracted set are exactly the numbers of paths they see. The resulting graph is a minor of $G$, so Lemma <a href="#lem:incidence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:incidence">21</a> implies that the number of exceptional vertices is at most $$\frac{t^{1+2\epsilon}|\mathcal C|}{B_*t}
 \le t^{2\epsilon}|\mathcal C|.$$ Apply this separately to $\mathcal A_T$ and $\mathcal B_T$. By <a href="#separate:path-count" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:path-count">[separate:path-count]</a>, the number at one snapshot is at most $6R_t t^{1+2\epsilon}$. Let $X$ be $X_0$ together with the exceptional vertices from all snapshots, including exceptional vertices outside $F_{\rm last}$. Then $$\begin{aligned}
 \label{separate:x-bound}
 |X|
 &\le 2R_t t^{1.06}+(13R_t+1)t
       +6R_t(R_t+1)t^{1+2\epsilon}\notag\\
 &=O(t^{1.06}\log^4t)+O(t^{1.01}\log^8t)
 \le t^{11/10}
\end{aligned}$$ for sufficiently large $t$, since $\epsilon=1/200$. Thus every required snapshot has been counted.

Put $Y=F_{\rm last}\setminus X$. The sets $X,Y$ are disjoint, and every vertex of $Y$ lies on a recorded path.

<a id="pm-h-24"></a>
###### Neighbors from outside the footprint.

<a id="separate:external-degree"></a>
Let $v\notin X\cup Y$. Then $v\notin F_{\rm last}$, so it was outside every recorded path union. Moreover, it belonged to the graph in which each system was minimized: every excluded set $F\setminus W$ or $F\cup R$ is contained in $F_{\rm last}$. By Lemma <a href="#lem:path-minimization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:path-minimization">32</a>, it has at most three neighbors on each path. Nonexceptionality at the final snapshot bounds the number of paths it sees by fewer than $B_*t$ in each collection. All stripped starts lie in $X_0$. Consequently $$\label{separate:external-degree}
 |N_G(v)\cap Y|\le6B_*t.$$

<a id="pm-h-25"></a>
###### Degeneracy inside the footprint.

Order the vertices of $Y$ by their round of first entry into the footprint. Within a round, put vertices on $\mathcal Q_1$ first, and then the remaining new vertices on $\mathcal Q_2$. This partitions $Y$ into at most two phases per round, because district vertices and all initial tips lie in $X_0$.

A vertex $v$ entering in a given round was outside that round’s old footprint $F$. If $v\in Y$, it was not exceptional at the snapshot $F$. For every earlier system, its forbidden vertices belong to $F$, while $v\notin F$; hence $v$ was eligible in the graph of that minimization and was outside its path union. The preceding argument therefore gives at most $6B_*t$ neighbors of $v$ in $Y$ from earlier rounds.

A first phase is contained in the union of at most $4t$ first-system paths with their starts removed. Lemma  <a href="#lem:path-minimization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:path-minimization">32</a> makes its induced graph $8t$-degenerate. A second phase is contained in the union of $2t$ minimizing second-system paths, so its induced graph is $4t$-degenerate, and in particular $8t$-degenerate. These are assertions about the induced graphs in $G$: all vertices of the relevant phase belong to the graph used for that minimization, which was an induced subgraph of $G$.

Finally, a vertex in the second phase of a round lies outside the entire first-system union and outside the old footprint. It therefore belongs to $G-(F\setminus W)$. Lemma <a href="#lem:path-minimization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:path-minimization">32</a> bounds its neighbors in the first phase by $3(4t)=12t$.

In any nonempty subgraph of $G[Y]$, select the latest represented phase and a vertex of degree at most $8t$ within that phase. It has no neighbors in a later represented phase, at most $12t$ neighbors in an earlier phase of the same round, and at most $6B_*t$ neighbors in earlier rounds. Hence $G[Y]$ is $(6B_*+20)t$-degenerate.

Equations <a href="#separate:x-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:x-bound">[separate:x-bound]</a> and <a href="#separate:external-degree" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:external-degree">[separate:external-degree]</a> now verify every hypothesis of Lemma <a href="#lem:additive-deletion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:additive-deletion">19</a>, with $d=6B_*+20$. It follows that $$\ell(G-X-Y)\ge\ell(G)-c_ft.$$ Since $F_{\rm last}\subseteq X\cup Y$, the graph $G-F_{\rm last}$ contains $G-X-Y$ as an induced subgraph. Monotonicity of list chromatic number proves the assertion. For the initial footprint the same proof has $Y=\varnothing$ and $X=W_0$. ◻

</details>

<details id="proof-stmt-separate-footprint-2"><summary>Proof of stmt-separate-footprint</summary>

<a id="separate:ch"></a>
<a id="separate:S"></a>
*Proof of Lemma <a href="#lem:separability" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:separability">34</a>.* Let $K_0=10^5\gamma$ be the integer fixed in Lemma <a href="#lem:small-woven" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:small-woven">31</a>, and put $k=K_0t$. Let $D_{K_0}$ be supplied by Lemma <a href="#lem:district" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:district">23</a>. Use $c_f$ from <a href="#separate:cf" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:cf">[separate:cf]</a>, put $$\label{separate:ch}
 c_h=c_f+6(K_0+1)+2,$$ and let $c_0=4L+5$ be the deletion constant for $d=0$. Choose a positive integer $S$ satisfying $$\begin{aligned}
 \label{separate:S}
 S&>c_h+K_0+2,\notag\\
 2S-c_f&>6(K_0+1)+2,\\
 2S-c_h-1-c_0&>2D_{K_0}+3.\notag
\end{aligned}$$ These choices involve only constants already fixed. We then take $t$ sufficiently large for Lemmas <a href="#lem:district" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:district">23</a>, <a href="#lem:small-woven" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:small-woven">31</a>, <a href="#lem:additive-deletion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:additive-deletion">19</a>, and <a href="#separate:footprint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="separate:footprint">35</a> with the fixed parameters used below, and for all displayed size inequalities in the construction.

Suppose that $r=\ell(G)\ge2St$, $h(G)<t$, but no two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs of $G$ both have list chromatic number at least $r-St$. We will construct a $K_t$ model.

<a id="pm-h-26"></a>
###### Labels, rounds, and invariants.

<a id="separate:s"></a>
Partition the label set $\{1,\ldots,t\}$ into $m_0$ nonempty blocks, each of size at most $\lceil t/m_0\rceil$. Schedule one round for each individual block and one for each unordered pair of distinct blocks. There are $R_t$ rounds. The labels treated in a round form a set $I$, which is either a block or the union of its two assigned blocks. Its size $s$ satisfies, for sufficiently large $t$, $$\label{separate:s}
 1\le s\le2\left\lceil\frac{t}{m_0}\right\rceil
 \le2\left\lceil\frac{t}{(\log t)^2}\right\rceil
 \le t.$$ Every pair of distinct labels occurs together in a scheduled round.

At the start of a round we maintain the following data.

1.  Pairwise disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets $B_1,\ldots,B_t$, with all adjacencies obtained in earlier rounds.

2.  A footprint $F$ containing these sets and arising from the history rules of Lemma <a href="#separate:footprint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="separate:footprint">35</a>. It retains all vertices of every district and of both original minimizing path systems from every completed round.

3.  A $k$-connected induced region $H$ with $$\ell(H)\ge r-c_ht,\qquad V(H)\cap F=W,$$ where $W=\{w_1,\ldots,w_t\}$ consists of distinct tips with $w_j\in B_j$.

In particular, no vertex of $H-W$ belongs to an earlier footprint. The distinction between the footprint and the sets $B_j$ is useful: unused path vertices remain in the footprint and are accounted for by Lemma <a href="#separate:footprint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="separate:footprint">35</a>.

The inequalities in <a href="#separate:S" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:S">[separate:S]</a> imply $r>6k$. Lemma <a href="#lem:list-extraction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:list-extraction">17</a> supplies a $k$-connected induced subgraph $H$ with $\ell(H)\ge r-6k\ge r-c_ht$. It has more than $k\ge t$ vertices. Choose distinct tips $w_j$ there and initialize $B_j=\{w_j\}$ and $F=W$.

<a id="pm-h-27"></a>
###### Two districts and the first minimizing system.

Consider a round with label set $I$ of size $s$. Deleting its current tips gives $$\ell(H-W)\ge r-(c_h+1)t.$$ Corollary <a href="#density:list-district" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="density:list-district">24</a> states that if $\ell(P)>2D_{K_0}t+2$ and $h(P)<t$, then $P$ contains an induced $k$-connected district of order at most $t^{1.06}$.

First obtain such a district $J\subseteq H-W$. Delete it using Lemma <a href="#lem:additive-deletion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:additive-deletion">19</a> with $X=V(J)$ and $Y=\varnothing$, losing at most $c_0t$. The remaining list chromatic number is at least $$r-(c_h+1+c_0)t
 \ge(2S-c_h-1-c_0)t
 >(2D_{K_0}+3)t>2D_{K_0}t+2.$$ The same district consequence supplies a second district $D\subseteq H-W-J$. Both $J,D$ are $k$-connected and have order at most $t^{1.06}$, and both are disjoint from $F$. Choose distinct roots $R_J=\{u_j:j\in I\}$ in $J$, and put $$Z=W\cup R_J,\qquad |Z|=t+s\le2t.$$

<a id="separate:intermediate-loss"></a>
The graph $H$ is a subgraph of $G-(F\setminus W)$, is $2|Z|$-connected, and contains the disjoint source and target sets $Z,D$. Also $|D|>k\ge2|Z|$. Lemma <a href="#lem:double-packing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:double-packing">26</a> therefore gives a feasible double system. Among all such systems in the full induced graph <a id="separate:first-domain"></a>$$\label{separate:first-domain}
 G-(F\setminus W)$$ choose a minimum-total-length system $\mathcal Q_1$. Its only intersections with $F$ are its prescribed starts in $W$. Set $$F^-=F\cup V(J)\cup V(D)\cup V(\mathcal Q_1).$$ The history ending with this first system satisfies Lemma <a href="#separate:footprint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="separate:footprint">35</a>, and hence $$\label{separate:intermediate-loss}
 \ell(G-F^-)\ge r-c_ft.$$

<a id="pm-h-28"></a>
###### The next region and the second minimizing system.

<a id="separate:new-region-list"></a>
By <a href="#separate:S" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:S">[separate:S]</a>, the right side of <a href="#separate:intermediate-loss" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:intermediate-loss">[separate:intermediate-loss]</a> is greater than $6(K_0+1)t$. Lemma <a href="#lem:list-extraction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:list-extraction">17</a> gives a $(K_0+1)t$-connected induced region $H'\subseteq G-F^-$ with $$\label{separate:new-region-list}
 \ell(H')\ge r-\bigl(c_f+6(K_0+1)\bigr)t.$$

We claim that $|V(H')\cap V(H)|\ge k$. Otherwise deleting this intersection from $H'$ gives an induced subgraph disjoint from $H$, of list chromatic number at least $$r-\bigl(c_f+6(K_0+1)+K_0\bigr)t\ge r-St.$$ The other graph $H$ has list chromatic number at least $r-c_ht\ge r-St$. This contradicts the supposition on $G$.

<a id="separate:second-domain"></a>
It follows that the graph induced by $V(H)\cup V(H')$ is $k$-connected. After deleting fewer than $k$ vertices, each of its two regions is connected and at least one vertex of their intersection survives. This union meets $F$ only in $W$. Deleting $Z=W\cup R_J$ leaves a graph of connectivity at least $$k-|Z|\ge(K_0-2)t\ge2t,$$ contained in the induced graph $$\label{separate:second-domain}
 G-(F\cup R_J).$$ Neither $H'$ nor $D$ meets $Z$, these two endpoint sets are disjoint, and each has more than $2t$ vertices. Lemma <a href="#lem:packing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packing">25</a> supplies $2t$ disjoint paths between them.

<a id="separate:region-footprint"></a>
Choose $\mathcal Q_2$ of minimum total length among all $2t$-path systems from arbitrary distinct vertices of $H'$ to arbitrary distinct vertices of $D$, in the full graph <a href="#separate:second-domain" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:second-domain">[separate:second-domain]</a>. This is an unpaired minimization. Its paths meet $H'$ and $D$ only at their respective ends. Let $T'\subseteq V(H')$ be their $2t$ starting vertices, and put $$F^+=F^-\cup V(\mathcal Q_2).$$ In particular, $$\label{separate:region-footprint}
 V(H')\cap F^+=T'.$$ This completes another round of the history in Lemma <a href="#separate:footprint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="separate:footprint">35</a>.

<a id="pm-h-29"></a>
###### Combining the systems and inserting the district model.

The sets $Z,V(H'),V(D)$ are pairwise disjoint. The first system avoids $H'$, since it lies in $F^-$; the second avoids $Z$, by its domain <a href="#separate:second-domain" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:second-domain">[separate:second-domain]</a>. Lemma <a href="#lem:combine" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:combine">33</a>, with $m=t$, gives $$q=|Z|+t=2t+s\le3t$$ vertex-disjoint paths to distinct vertices of $D$, one from each vertex of $Z$ and one from each vertex of a selected set $W^+\subseteq T'$ of size $t$. They meet $D,H'$ only at their designated ends, use only vertices of the two systems, and meet $F$ only in the $W$-ends. In particular, they do not visit the unused starts $T'\setminus W^+$. Assign $W^+=\{w_1^+,\ldots,w_t^+\}$ bijectively to the labels.

By <a href="#separate:s" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:s">[separate:s]</a> and Lemma <a href="#lem:small-woven" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:small-woven">31</a>, the district $J$ is $(s,3t)$-woven. Apply Lemma <a href="#lem:rerouting" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:rerouting">29</a> to the $q$ combined paths and the roots $R_J$. It produces in $J$ a rooted $K_s$ model with bags $C_j$, $j\in I$, and reroutes the combined paths without changing their ends. Each root $u_j$ was already the endpoint of its own path. Thus the model meets the paths only at these roots, each on its corresponding path and in its corresponding bag.

The new vertices of the rerouted paths lie in $J\subseteq F^+$. Since $J$ is disjoint from $F,H',D$, all the previous endpoint-only intersection statements with these sets persist. All rerouted paths and all bags $C_j$ lie in $F^+$. We continue to record the original minimizing systems in the history; the rerouted paths are used only to extend the label bags.

<a id="pm-h-30"></a>
###### Grouping in $D$ and restoring the invariants.

For each label $j$, group the terminals in $D$ belonging to the paths from $w_j$, from $w_j^+$, and, if $j\in I$, from $u_j$. These groups partition the $q$ distinct terminals. Since $$\gamma q\le3\gamma t\le K_0t,$$ Theorem <a href="#thm:grouping" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:grouping">5</a> supplies pairwise disjoint connected sets $E_1,\ldots,E_t$ in $D$ containing their respective groups. For the next region put $$H^+=H'-(T'\setminus W^+).$$ Figure <a href="#fig:separability-round" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:separability-round">1</a> now shows how these pieces fit into one extended label bag.

<figure id="fig:separability-round">

<figcaption>A separability round, shown schematically. The upper arrows represent families of paths; the two families may intersect, and their entire vertex sets remain in the footprint. Below, $E_{j}$ joins label $j$’s path ends in $D$. The region $H^{+}$ is obtained from $H′$ by removing unused starts; it meets the footprint exactly in the new tips $W^{+}$.</figcaption>
</figure>



Extend $B_j$ by the two or three corresponding paths, by $E_j$, and by $C_j$ when $j\in I$. The resulting set $B_j^+$ is connected: its old bag contains $w_j$; the paths join every attached piece to $E_j$; and it contains the new tip $w_j^+$. The sets $B_j^+$ are pairwise disjoint. Indeed, the old bags are disjoint and meet the added paths only at their own $W$-ends; the paths are disjoint; the sets $E_j$ are disjoint and meet paths only at the designated terminals; and the bags $C_j$ are disjoint, lie outside $F\cup D$, and meet paths only at their own roots. All these sets lie in $F^+$. Old adjacencies persist because $B_j\subseteq B_j^+$, and every pair of labels in $I$ gains an adjacency through its bags in the district model.

It remains to check the next-region invariant. Exactly $t$ vertices were deleted from the $(K_0+1)t$-connected graph $H'$, so $H^+$ is $K_0t$-connected. By <a href="#separate:new-region-list" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:new-region-list">[separate:new-region-list]</a> and <a href="#separate:ch" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:ch">[separate:ch]</a>, $$\ell(H^+)
 \ge r-\bigl(c_f+6(K_0+1)+1\bigr)t
 \ge r-c_ht.$$ Equation <a href="#separate:region-footprint" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="separate:region-footprint">[separate:region-footprint]</a> gives $$V(H^+)\cap F^+=W^+.$$ Thus $F^+,H^+,W^+$, and the bags $B_j^+$ restore every invariant for the next round.

After all $R_t$ rounds, every pair of labels has an adjacency. The $t$ disjoint connected label bags therefore form a $K_t$ model in $G$, contradicting $h(G)<t$. This proves Lemma <a href="#lem:separability" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:separability">34</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="sec:recursion"></a>
### Recursive weaving and the universal bound

The recursive use of woven districts follows the framework of Postle (Postle 2020, sec. 6) <a id="pm-cite-43"></a>[[Postle2020](#ref-Postle2020)] and Delcourt and Postle (Delcourt and Postle 2025, sec. 7) <a id="pm-cite-44"></a>[[DelcourtPostle2021](#ref-DelcourtPostle2021)]. We now use separability to replace the successive small steps of the preceding section by a recursion with a fixed shrinkage factor.

<a id="stmt-thm-recursive-woven"></a>
<div id="thm:recursive-woven" class="theorem">

**Theorem 36**. *There are absolute positive integers $K,Q$ such that, for every integer $a\ge1$, every $Ka$-connected graph $P$ with $\ell(P)\ge Qa$ is $(a,3a)$-woven.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-recursive-woven"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-recursive-woven</summary>

*Proof.* The main inductive step concerns $h(P)<64a$ and sufficiently large $a$. It separates the paths for prescribed pairs from the clique-model construction. Give each root and each end of a noncoincident pair its own neighboring proxy outside the original terminal set, with all proxies distinct, and delete the original terminals. Choose a minimum-total-length system of two paths per proxy to a small highly connected district $D$. Deleting the proxies, $D$, and these paths costs only $O(a)$ in list chromatic number. We can therefore extract a highly connected region $H'$ disjoint from the first path system. Further connections from $H'$ to $D$ and Lemma <a href="#lem:combine" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:combine">33</a> produce disjoint paths from all proxies and from a set $W$ of $a$ vertices of $H'$ to $D$, meeting $H'$ only at $W$. It then suffices to build a clique model rooted at $W$ inside $H'$: grouping the path ends in $D$ attaches the model to the root proxies and completes the prescribed pair paths.

For this internal model, divide the labels of $W$ into three blocks. Separability and connectivity extraction supply three disjoint districts for recursive calls, one for each pair of blocks. A call needs at most $2\lceil a/3\rceil$ roots. Each label receives two bags to be joined to its vertex of $W$. The $2a$ joining paths may pass through the recursive districts; wovenness lets us reroute them while constructing the child models, keeping the retained bags disjoint from the paths except at their designated roots. Every pair of labels shares a district and hence receives an adjacency.

<a id="recursive:K"></a>
<a id="recursive:shrink"></a>
<a id="recursive:Q-induction"></a>
<a id="recursive:Q-separation"></a>
<a id="recursive:Q-base"></a>
We specify the order of the constants first. Fix all constants in the preceding sections, including $L,C_*,B_*,K_0,D_{K_0}$, the deletion constants $c_d$, and the separability constant $S$. Choose an integer $K\ge100$ such that $$\label{recursive:K}
 K-14>128D_{K_0}.$$ Choose an absolute integer $a_0\ge24$ so large that all sufficiently-large parameter conclusions used below hold with $t=64a$ whenever $a>a_0$. Enlarge $a_0$ if necessary so that $$\label{recursive:shrink}
 a'=2\lceil a/3\rceil\le3a/4\qquad(a>a_0),$$ and $t^{1.06}+7a\le t^{11/10}$ for $t=64a$, $a>a_0$. All these requirements involve only constants already fixed, and none involves $Q$. Finally choose an integer $Q$ satisfying $$\begin{aligned}
 Q/4&>10+64(c_{42}+6K_0+2S)+(9/2)K,
       \label{recursive:Q-induction}\\
 Q&>10+64(c_{42}+6K_0+3S),
       \label{recursive:Q-separation}\\
 Q&>128C_*\log(128a_0)+1.
       \label{recursive:Q-base}
\end{aligned}$$ We prove the assertion by strong induction on $a$.

<a id="pm-h-32"></a>
###### Separating the terminal roles.

Fix $a$ distinct roots and at most $3a$ pairs as in Definition <a href="#def:woven" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:woven">28</a>. Let $Z_0$ be their union, so $|Z_0|\le7a$. For each root, and for each end of each noncoincident pair, choose a neighbor outside $Z_0$ as its *proxy*. All proxies are distinct, even for different roles of the same original vertex. This is possible greedily because $\delta(P)\ge Ka$ and fewer than $14a$ vertices are forbidden at any choice. Coincident pairs will ultimately use trivial paths at their original vertices and need no proxies.

Put $G=P-Z_0$ and let $Z$ be the proxy set. Then <a id="recursive:proxy-bounds"></a>$$\label{recursive:proxy-bounds}
 a\le|Z|\le7a,\qquad
 G\text{ is }(K-7)a\text{-connected},\qquad
 \ell(G)\ge Qa-7a.$$ It suffices to find in $G$ a clique model rooted at the root proxies and paths for the other proxy pairs, with all model bags and all these paths pairwise disjoint. Adding the proxy edges and the original vertices then restores precisely the root–path coincidences allowed by wovenness. Different prescribed pairs have no common original endpoint; a coincident pair at a root meets only that root’s expanded bag.

<a id="pm-h-33"></a>
###### A large minor and the finite base range.

Set $t=64a$. If $h(P)\ge t$, delete from a $K_t$ model every bag meeting $Z_0$. This leaves a $K_{57a}$ model in $G$. Since $57a\ge4|Z|$ and $(K-7)a\ge2|Z|$, Lemma <a href="#lem:rooting" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:rooting">27</a> gives a clique model rooted at all of $Z$. Retain the root-proxy bags. For each other proxy pair, a path through its two bags and an edge between them joins the pair. These paths and the retained bags are disjoint because all proxies and their bags are distinct. This proves the required conclusion in the large-minor case, for every $a$.

Suppose $h(P)<64a$. Lemma <a href="#lem:coarse-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:coarse-density">20</a> gives $$\ell(P)\le128C_*a\log(128a)+1.$$ For $1\le a\le a_0$ this is strictly less than $Qa$ by <a href="#recursive:Q-base" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="recursive:Q-base">[recursive:Q-base]</a>. Thus the minor-free case is impossible throughout the base range. We may henceforth assume $a>a_0$.

<a id="pm-h-34"></a>
###### A junction district and a fresh region.

Every vertex of $G-Z$ has degree at least $(K-14)a$, which is greater than $2D_{K_0}t$ by <a href="#recursive:K" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="recursive:K">[recursive:K]</a>. In particular this graph is nonempty and has density greater than $D_{K_0}t$. Apply Lemma <a href="#lem:district" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:district">23</a> to find a $K_0t$-connected district $D\subseteq G-Z$ with $|V(D)|\le t^{1.06}$.

The connectivity of $G$ and the order of $D$ permit two paths per proxy from $Z$ to distinct vertices of $D$, with only the prescribed repeated starts in common, by Lemma <a href="#lem:double-packing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:double-packing">26</a>. Choose such a system $\mathcal Q_1$ of minimum total length in $G$. It has at most $14a$ paths. Put $$X=Z\cup V(D),\qquad Y=V(\mathcal Q_1)\setminus X.$$ We have $|X|\le t^{11/10}$ by the choice of $a_0$. Lemma <a href="#lem:path-minimization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:path-minimization">32</a> gives $28a$-degeneracy of $G[Y]$ and at most $42a$ neighbors in $Y$ for every vertex outside $X\cup Y$. These bounds are at most $42t$, so Lemma <a href="#lem:additive-deletion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:additive-deletion">19</a> with parameter $42$ gives <a id="recursive:after-paths"></a>$$\label{recursive:after-paths}
 \ell(G-X-Y)\ge Qa-7a-c_{42}t.$$ By <a href="#recursive:Q-separation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="recursive:Q-separation">[recursive:Q-separation]</a> the right-hand side exceeds $6K_0t$. Lemma <a href="#lem:list-extraction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:list-extraction">17</a> therefore supplies a $K_0t$-connected induced subgraph $H'\subseteq G-X-Y$ such that <a id="recursive:Hprime"></a>$$\label{recursive:Hprime}
 \ell(H')\ge Qa-7a-(c_{42}+6K_0)t.$$

In $G-Z$, the sets $H'$ and $D$ have order greater than $K_0t$, and the connectivity is at least $(K-14)a>2a$. Hence there are $2a$ disjoint $H'$-to-$D$ paths. Truncate them at their last visit to $H'$ and their first subsequent visit to $D$, so they have no internal vertex in either set. They avoid $Z$. Lemma <a href="#lem:combine" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:combine">33</a>, applied to these paths and $\mathcal Q_1$, gives disjoint paths to $D$ from all proxies in $Z$ and from a set $W$ of $a$ distinct vertices of $H'$. These paths meet $H'$ and $D$ only at their appropriate ends.

It is now enough to construct a clique model rooted at $W$ entirely inside $H'$. Indeed, in $D$ group the terminal ends of the outside paths as follows: pair each root proxy with a different member of $W$, and pair the other proxies as prescribed. There are at most $|Z|+a\le8a$ terminals, so Theorem <a href="#thm:grouping" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:grouping">5</a> applies because $K_0t\ge8\gamma a$. These disjoint groups and the outside paths attach the rooted model to the root proxies and supply all other required paths. The model inside $H'$ has no unwanted intersection with the outside paths, since their only vertices in $H'$ are precisely $W$.

<a id="pm-h-35"></a>
###### Three recursive districts.

For each $w\in W$ choose two neighbors in $H'-W$, all $2a$ choices distinct. Minimum degree at least $K_0t$ permits this greedy choice. Let $N$ be their set and put $H''=H'-W-N$. Then <a id="recursive:r0"></a>$$\label{recursive:r0}
 \ell(H'')\ge r_0:=Qa-10a-(c_{42}+6K_0)t.$$ Equation <a href="#recursive:Q-separation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="recursive:Q-separation">[recursive:Q-separation]</a> gives $r_0>3St$. Apply Lemma <a href="#lem:separability" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:separability">34</a> to $H''$, and then to one of the two resulting subgraphs. The first application is legal because $\ell(H'')\ge r_0>2St$. Each of its subgraphs has list chromatic number at least $r_0-St>2St$, making the second application legal as well. We obtain three disjoint subgraphs each of list chromatic number at least $r_0-2St$.

Take $a'=2\lceil a/3\rceil$. After the loss of $2St$ to separability, each subgraph must still pay $6Ka'$ for connectivity extraction and retain $Qa'$ for the recursive call. If $A=10+64(c_{42}+6K_0+2S)$, then $$\begin{aligned}
 r_0-2St-6Ka'-Qa'
 &=Q(a-a')-Aa-6Ka'\\
 &\ge\bigl[Q/4-A-(9/2)K\bigr]a>0
\end{aligned}$$ by <a href="#recursive:shrink" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="recursive:shrink">[recursive:shrink]</a> and <a href="#recursive:Q-induction" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="recursive:Q-induction">[recursive:Q-induction]</a>. In particular $r_0-2St>6Ka'$, and list extraction in each subgraph produces disjoint $Ka'$-connected induced districts $J_1,J_2,J_3$ with list chromatic number at least $Qa'$. Since $a'<a$, induction makes each district $(a',3a')$-woven.

Partition the labels of $W$ into three nonempty blocks $B_1,B_2,B_3$, each of size at most $\lceil a/3\rceil$. Assign one district to each pair of blocks, relabeling them $J_{12},J_{13},J_{23}$ accordingly. In its district, designate a distinct root for each label of the corresponding two blocks, and add arbitrary distinct padding roots to bring the total to $a'$. The districts have enough vertices for this choice. Every label has exactly two designated roots, in different districts; every pair of labels occurs together in at least one district, including two labels in the same block; see Figure <a href="#fig:three-districts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:three-districts">2</a>.

<figure id="fig:three-districts">

<figcaption>The three recursive districts. The blocks $B_{1}, B_{2}, B_{3}$ partition the labels, and a label has one designated root in each of the two districts receiving its block. Arrows indicate label assignments, not graph edges. Every pair of labels is represented together in a district.</figcaption>
</figure>

<a id="pm-figsrc-fig-three-districts"></a>
**Figure source and visual witness** (`fig:three-districts`)

Visual witness description of PDF page 39 (generated from the PDF page, not source text):

```text
A bipartite-style assignment diagram between two horizontal rows of rounded rectangular boxes:
- Top row: three boxes labeled "B_1", "B_2", and "B_3".
- Bottom row: three boxes labeled "J_{12} : B_1 \cup B_2", "J_{13} : B_1 \cup B_3", and "J_{23} : B_2 \cup B_3".
- Directed arrows indicating assignments:
  - From B_1 to J_{12} : B_1 \cup B_2 (downward) and to J_{13} : B_1 \cup B_3 (down-right).
  - From B_2 to J_{12} : B_1 \cup B_2 (down-left) and to J_{23} : B_2 \cup B_3 (down-right).
  - From B_3 to J_{13} : B_1 \cup B_3 (down-left) and to J_{23} : B_2 \cup B_3 (downward).
```

Inside $H'-W$, join the two chosen neighbors of each $w$ to its two designated roots, respectively, using disjoint paths. This is an application of Theorem <a href="#thm:grouping" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:grouping">5</a> to $4a$ distinct terminals: the neighbors lie in $N$, while the districts were chosen in $H''$ and hence avoid $N$. The connectivity is at least $K_0t-a\ge4\gamma a$. There are $2a$ paths. Apply Lemma <a href="#lem:rerouting" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:rerouting">29</a> successively in the three districts to incorporate their rooted clique models while retaining these path ends. Each district has sufficient weaving capacity, since $$2a\le3a'=6\lceil a/3\rceil.$$ Discard all padding bags. Each designated root remains an endpoint of its path; the retained bags meet the rerouted paths only at their own designated roots. Since the districts are disjoint, later rerouting does not introduce an intersection in a previously retained bag.

For each $w$, unite its two designated bags with their respective paths, the two edges to $w$, and $w$ itself. The resulting $a$ sets are connected and disjoint, rooted at $W$. Two labels have an edge between their sets because they occur together in one of the district clique models. This constructs the required rooted $K_a$ model inside $H'$ and completes the induction. ◻

</details>

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-recursive-woven-2"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-recursive-woven</summary>

<a id="recursive:final-minor-free"></a>
*Proof of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>.* Let $K,Q$ be as in Theorem <a href="#thm:recursive-woven" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:recursive-woven">36</a>. We first show that, for every integer $t\ge2$, $$\label{recursive:final-minor-free}
 h(G)<t\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\ell(G)\le(Q+6K)t.$$ Otherwise Lemma <a href="#lem:list-extraction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:list-extraction">17</a>, with connectivity parameter $Kt$, gives a $Kt$-connected induced subgraph $P$ with $\ell(P)\ge\ell(G)-6Kt>Qt$. Theorem <a href="#thm:recursive-woven" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:recursive-woven">36</a> makes $P$ $(t,3t)$-woven. Its order is greater than $Kt\ge t$, so we may choose $t$ roots and no pairs. Wovenness then supplies a $K_t$ model, contradicting $h(G)<t$.

For a nonempty graph, $h(G)\ge1$. Taking $t=h(G)+1\le2h(G)$ in <a href="#recursive:final-minor-free" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="recursive:final-minor-free">[recursive:final-minor-free]</a> proves $$\ell(G)\le2(Q+6K)h(G).$$ Thus the absolute integer $C=2(Q+6K)$ has all the claimed uniformity. The finite base range was covered before the induction began, so no small-parameter exception remains. ◻

</details>
